extracted.intended_audience: Indian patent applicants, patent agents, and practitioners preparing and filing PCT (international) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting clear patent claims and preparing/filing an International (PCT) patent application from India, including Receiving Office formalities, required contents, language/translation rules, fees, search/examination stages, amendments, and entry into the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must have precise, well-recognized meanings for a person skilled in the art; vague terms (e.g. 'near-amorphous') that leave the reader in doubt render the claim unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'near-amorphous film comprising ZrO2' is vague and unclear. Avoid terms without a precise technical meaning or that would leave the skilled person uncertain about the technical feature referred to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ambiguous claim syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim wording should be unambiguous so that it cannot be read in more than one sensible way (e.g. scope should not leave it unclear whether multiple components are both made of a material or only one is).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A Diesel engine comprising an engine block and a cylinder head made of an Aluminum-Titanium alloy having a melting point between 1000 K and 1100 K' — syntax can be read as either both parts are made of the alloy or only the cylinder head is. Draft claims to remove such syntactic ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not claim by result when technical features are available
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must define subject-matter in terms of technical features, not merely the desired result or performance, when it is possible to state how the effect is achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A digital photo-camera ... characterized in that it is adapted to operate at temperatures down to 200 K' defines by the object to be achieved rather than the technical features (materials, insulation, etc.). Where concrete technical features can be given, do so rather than claim purely by outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must define the subject matter, be clear and concise, and be supported
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must define the subject-matter of the invention for which protection is sought; they must be clear and concise and fully supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT claim-drafting requirements are largely similar to those of most national patent Offices. Ensure clarity, conciseness, and full support in the description to avoid objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description sufficiency and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description should: repeat the title; specify the technical field; indicate background art (prior art); disclose the technical problem and its solution; state advantageous effects over known technology; briefly describe drawings; set forth the best mode contemplated and other modes; and indicate industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract purpose and length
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is intended solely as technical information and cannot be used to interpret the scope of protection; it should be a concise summary within preferably 50 to 150 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft the abstract to allow clear understanding of the technical problem, the gist of the solution provided by the invention, and the principal use. Do not rely on the abstract for claim interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings required only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required only where necessary for the understanding of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically needed for engineering-type inventions; not required when an invention cannot be drawn (e.g., many chemical inventions). Follow drawing requirements similar to most patent Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sequence listing part is filed only on electronic medium under new Section 801, a designated Office may require a paper copy for national phase; existing provisions for written form continue for applicants not using new Section 801.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International applications filed under new Section 801 may only be filed with Receiving Offices prepared to accept them and on electronic media specified by those Offices. The basic fee calculation may depend on total number of sheets including sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request form contents and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Request (PCT/RO/101) must contain a petition to process the International Application, title, applicant/inventor/agent data, and signature; may be on printed form or computer printout (with electronic copy when required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be signed by applicant or agent; where multiple applicants exist each must sign or provide power of attorney. Optional indications (e.g., priority claim) may be included. Triplicate copies where required; online filing and PCT-SAFE formats possible where supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for according international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: An international filing date is accorded when the Receiving Office finds the application in order per Article 11 at time of receipt; certain minimal elements must be present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required elements include: (a) an indication it is intended to be an International Application; (b) designation of at least one Contracting State; (c) name of the applicant in a form allowing identity establishment; (d) a part which on its face appears to be a claim or claims. If corrections are required and filed later, the filing date may be the date of the correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Receiving Office (RO) formality check
rubrics_metrics.description: The RO checks only prescribed formal and physical requirements; it does not examine substantive issues such as sufficiency of disclosure or unity of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RO checks elementary requirements specified in the Treaty necessary for international filing and reasonably uniform publication; detailed substantive issues are reserved for search/examining authorities or national offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: RO handling of defects and effect on filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain defects may be corrected without affecting the international filing date; others may require invitation and correction, failing which the application can be considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical defects correctable without affecting filing date: non-payment or partial payment of fees; lack of signature of the request; lack of title; lack of an abstract; physical defects. For some defects the RO will invite correction; compliance within the Regulations may preserve the filing date; failure can lead to withdrawal. Rule 16b provides for inviting payment of missing fees with late payment option before withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of filing and translation obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Application must be filed in a language accepted by the Receiving Office; if the RO accepts the language but the chosen International Searching Authority does not, the applicant must furnish a translation within one month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For India, RO accepts English or Hindi. If applicant fails to furnish a required translation within applicable time limits (or pay for late furnishing if invited), the International Application may be considered withdrawn subject to safeguards. The request must always be filed in a language accepted by the RO and also one of the seven publication languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of record and search copies and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The RO must transmit the record copy to the International Bureau and the search copy to the International Searching Authority; timing requirements apply to ensure timely publication and search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record copy must be mailed promptly and in any case not later than five days prior to the expiration of the 13th month from the priority date. The search copy is normally transmitted at the same time except where search fees were not paid on time.

rubrics_metrics.name: International search: responsible authorities and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-quality international search report is established by the International Searching Authority (ISA); for Indian applicants competent ISAs include AT, AU, EP, CN, US, SE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no priority is claimed, the ISR is available within nine months from the international filing date; if priority is claimed, usually during the 16th month from the priority date. ISR is normally available before publication, allowing applicant options (e.g., withdraw before publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT fees: types, payment deadlines, and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees include Transmittal Fee (to RO), International Fee (to IB), Supplement per excess sheets, and Search Fee (to ISA); amounts and due dates vary and are generally due within one month from receipt of the International Application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmittal fee compensates RO; amount set by RO and due within one month. International Fee covers IB work; Search Fee covers ISA work. Failure to pay or underpayment can be corrected under Rule 16b after invitation, possibly with a late payment fee. Indian applicants typically remit consolidated USD amounts by demand draft to the Controller of Patents' designated account as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring key time limits and events
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should supervise a limited set of crucial time limits and events during the international phase to preserve rights and make informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor: (i) receipt confirmation by RO; (ii) time limits for payment of fees; (iii) notification from IB confirming record copy (Form PCT/IB/301) and correctness of designations (confirm precautionary designations within 15 months from priority date if needed); (iv) after ISR receipt, decide whether to file a demand for international preliminary examination before 19 months; (v) decide whether to file amended claims under Article 19 within applicable time; (vi) monitor receipt in 19th month of Form PCT/IB/308 confirming publication; (vii) enter national phase before expiration of 30/31 months by paying national fees and furnishing required translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during international phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and other parts of the application can be amended at various stages under specified PCT provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under Article 19, claims can be amended once with effect in all designated States. Individual amendments before each designated Office are permitted in the national phase (Articles 28 or 41). Under Article 34(2) during Chapter II (international preliminary examination) all parts (description, claims, drawings) may be amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Preliminary Examination optional use and benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a demand for international preliminary examination (Chapter II) is optional and provides an international preliminary examination report/opinion on patentability criteria and other benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include: (i) an opinion on usual criteria of patentability before incurring national-phase costs; (ii) assistance in adapting the application to ISR results; (iii) the possibility to amend all parts of the application for all elected Offices; (iv) an assessed probability of obtaining patents; and (v) potential cost savings if the report is negative and the applicant decides to abandon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal to prevent publication
rubrics_metrics.description: An International Application may be withdrawn at any time during the international phase; to prevent publication, the notice must reach the International Bureau before technical preparations for publication are completed (not later than 15 days before publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal can be conditional (effective only if publication can be prevented). Timing is crucial if preventing publication is the intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into the national phase and consequences of failure
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain protection in designated/elected States, the applicant must enter the national phase by performing prescribed acts within the national-phase time limits; failure to do so causes the International Application to lose effect in those States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry typically requires payment of national fees and furnishing translations (if required) before expiration of 30/31 months (jurisdiction-dependent). Failure has same consequences as withdrawal of a national application in those States (Article 24).
